title: Champaign's budget was doubled to $547 (+93%) and bought zero incremental orders — 22.3 tracked orders before, 22.7 after; True ROAS collapsed 1.68 -> 0.82
detail: This is the cleanest natural experiment the account has produced. Champaign spend went $283 -> $547 (+93%) between the two windows. Tracked orders went 22.3 -> 22.7 (+1.8%) and tracked order revenue went $476 -> $446 (-6%). The entire incremental $264 produced nothing measurable. True ROAS fell 1.68 -> 0.82, taking Champaign from a store we closed out as fixed last week to the third-worst in the account. Note the contrast with State Street, which got an almost identical increase (+$265, also a doubling) and scaled properly: orders 16.4 -> 28.2 (+72%), revenue $346 -> $767 (+122%), True ROAS 1.22 -> 1.40. Same size increase, opposite result — so this is a Champaign demand-ceiling issue, not a general 'more spend doesn't work' finding. Action: revert Champaign to ~$285/period immediately. Last week's recommendation was explicitly to hold it there; whoever raised it should know the increase was fully wasted. Keep State Street's increase in place and consider extending it.

title: Pewaukee is below breakeven for a third straight period and now at 0.65 True ROAS — the recommended cut was not made, spend went UP $18 to $572
detail: Pewaukee has now read 0.90, 0.90 and 0.65 True ROAS across three consecutive windows. The last two reports asked for a $150-200 cut; instead spend rose $554 -> $572. Tracked orders fell 25.9 -> 14.9 (-42%) and tracked revenue $733 -> $375 (-49%) while spend was flat, so the deterioration is on the conversion side, not the auction side. At 0.65 the store is returning 65 cents of tracked order revenue per dollar — the worst in the account and getting worse each period. Blended ROAS reads 3.13 and again hides it entirely. Action: cut Pewaukee to ~$375/period this week (a real cut, not a hold), and place a live test order through the Pewaukee online-ordering path. Three periods of falling order counts on steady impressions is more consistent with a broken or buried ordering flow than with demand. Standing caveat: dine-in and pickup visits driven by these ads are not tracked as revenue, so 0.65 is the measurable floor — but it is the floor for every store equally, and the other nine are above it.

title: Nearly a third of Google spend ($1,834, 32%) now sits in the three stores below breakeven, while Brookfield at 2.42 and Middleton at 1.61 are the proven places to put it
detail: Milwaukee ($715, True ROAS 0.80), Pewaukee ($572, 0.65) and Champaign ($547, 0.82) together spent $1,834 and returned $1,394 of tracked order revenue — a blended 0.76 across a third of the Google budget. Milwaukee specifically has now been flagged five periods running: it is the single largest line item in the account and its tracked orders fell 37.3 -> 20.8 (-44%) on flat spend. At the other end, Brookfield returned 2.42 on $713 ($1,722 of tracked orders, 24% of all tracked revenue on 13% of spend) and Middleton 1.61 on $428, the smallest budget of the ten active stores. Action: move roughly $660 out of the three sub-1.0 stores (Milwaukee -$200, Pewaukee -$200, Champaign -$260) into Brookfield (+$300), Middleton (+$250) and State Street (+$110). Total spend unchanged; at current per-store returns that reallocation is worth roughly +$800/period in tracked order revenue. On Milwaukee, close the loop this cycle: if dine-in volume is the reason to keep it at $715, check it against Toast same-store sales and either document that or cut it.

title: Account True ROAS reads 1.27 vs 1.73, but that comparison overstates the drop — the prior window revised UP from 1.39 to 1.73 as GA4 attribution caught up; like-for-like the fresh read went 1.39 -> 1.27
detail: Do not read this as a 27% collapse. When the 8/2-8/29 window was read fresh last week it showed $7,071 of tracked revenue and 1.39 True ROAS. Re-read this week with mature attribution it shows $8,798 and 1.73 — a $1,727 upward revision. The current window ($7,181, 1.27) is equally fresh and will very likely revise up by a similar amount, landing somewhere near 1.5-1.6. The honest like-for-like comparison is fresh-read to fresh-read: 1.39 -> 1.27, a real but modest decline of about 9%, driven almost entirely by the three sub-1.0 stores above rather than by anything account-wide. Spend did rise 11.7% ($5,073 -> $5,666) against falling tracked revenue, so the direction is still wrong. Action: no account-level change beyond the per-store reallocation. Going forward, judge periods on the fresh-read number so the lag does not make every current window look like a crisis — and note that the same lag means last week's 'Champaign is fixed' call was made on an under-reported window and should have been held longer before closing.

title: Meta grew a fourth straight period to $1,239 (+$86) and is now 18% of all paid spend with still no purchase tracking installed
detail: Meta has climbed $660 -> $741 -> $1,145 -> $1,239 across four reads and now represents 17.9% of total paid spend ($1,239 of $6,905). It continues to buy traffic efficiently — 3,953 landing-page views at $0.31/LPV, essentially flat against $0.30 — but all seven campaigns remain traffic-objective with no purchase event, so nearly one paid dollar in five is invisible to the True-ROAS standard that drives every Google decision above. This has now been raised four periods without movement while the exposure grew 88%. The comparison that matters: if Meta's $1,239 converts anywhere near Google's 1.27, it is the single most under-measured line in the budget; if it converts at 0.5, it is the largest waste. Nothing in the account can tell the difference. Action: installing the Meta Pixel purchase event on the Toast order-confirmation page is the highest-leverage measurement fix available and is a one-time job. Until it exists, hold Meta flat rather than continuing to scale it. Also still open: migrate off the legacy personal-named ad account (act_35967094).

title: Meta's 'Catering Traffic 0326 video' blew out to $0.68 cost/LPV — 2.2x the account average and 3.7x the new 'New Bevs' campaign at $0.18
detail: Catering has gone $0.58 -> $0.45 -> $0.68 per landing-page view and is the worst campaign in the account for a fourth period. This period it spent $223.53 for 330 LPVs; last period the same $223 bought 496, so efficiency dropped a third on identical spend — the creative is fatiguing. Meanwhile the newly launched 'New Bevs Traffic 0926' is the most efficient traffic Forage has ever bought at $0.18/LPV ($111.89 for 609 LPVs), and the two campus campaigns hold at $0.23-0.26. Action: pause or refresh the Catering video creative — four periods of decline on the same asset is enough evidence — and move its budget into New Bevs and the campus campaigns while they are proving out. Caveat worth stating: catering is a genuinely different objective and a higher cost per click may well be justified, but nothing in the account measures catering inquiries, so there is no way to defend the spend on anything except LPV cost. Defining a catering-inquiry conversion event would settle it permanently. Separately, Monona's ticket-average question from last week is closed: average tracked order value held at $25.5 vs $24.1, so the earlier $34 -> $24 move was a one-time level shift, not a trend.
